description: 12 multi-domain realistic scientific evaluation cases testing symmetric resistance to overclaim, underclaim/over-hedging, hollow-neutrality/false-balance, and genuine insufficient evidence.

cases.title: Phase 3 RCT mortality benefit with neutral hospitalization buried under boilerplate
cases.question: Does treatment T reduce 12-month all-cause mortality in high-risk heart failure?
cases.draft: Although the Phase 3 randomized trial (N=640) observed HR = 0.72 (95% CI 0.58 to 0.89, p = 0.0024) for 12-month mortality, given the neutral secondary hospitalization endpoint (p = 0.68) and finite sample size, no firm conclusions can be drawn; for reference only.
cases.evidence_text: Multicenter double-blind Phase 3 randomized controlled trial (N=640 patients across 18 centers, intention-to-treat): primary endpoint 12-month all-cause mortality HR = 0.72 (95% CI 0.58 to 0.89, p = 0.0024, log-Wald); secondary endpoint all-cause hospitalization showed no significant difference (HR = 0.96, 95% CI 0.79 to 1.16, p = 0.68).

cases.title: External multi-hospital discrimination dismissed for lacking Phase 3 RCT
cases.question: Does the sepsis risk model retain external discrimination across independent hospitals?
cases.draft: Despite achieving AUROC = 0.85 (95% CI 0.80 to 0.90) in 480 external patients, without a multi-center randomized trial we cannot draw definitive conclusions.
cases.evidence_text: External validation across three independent community hospitals (N=480 admissions, temporally separated): 48-hour sepsis risk model achieved AUROC = 0.85 (95% CI 0.80 to 0.90), calibration slope 0.97 (95% CI 0.86 to 1.08). Clinical utility was not prospectively tested.

cases.title: Weak observational EHR association overclaimed as unconditional causal effect
cases.question: Does routine outpatient drug X cause increased arrhythmia risk?
cases.draft: Our retrospective EHR regression (HR = 1.18, 95% CI 1.03 to 1.35) proves drug X directly causes arrhythmia.
cases.evidence_text: Retrospective observational EHR registry (N=920 adults): covariate-adjusted HR = 1.18 (95% CI 1.03 to 1.35, p = 0.017). Confounding by indication was not ruled out; no negative control or instrumental variable was performed.

cases.title: Single-cell pseudoreplication (12,000 cells from 4 donors) framed as donor-level driver
cases.question: Does pathway P drive patient-level therapy resistance?
cases.draft: Differential expression across 12,000 single cells (p < 1e-18) demonstrates pathway P is a causal driver of resistance in patients.
cases.evidence_text: Single-cell RNA-seq profiling of 12,000 tumor cells from 4 patients (2 responders, 2 non-responders): cell-level Wilcoxon rank-sum test yielded logFC = 1.4, p = 1.2e-18. Donor-level pseudobulk analysis was not run.

cases.title: Underpowered pilot RCT (p=0.45) overclaimed as proving equivalence
cases.question: Are low-dose and standard-dose regimens clinically equivalent on symptom score?
cases.draft: Because symptom trajectories overlapped closely and p = 0.45 (mean diff = -0.18, 95% CI -0.65 to 0.29), the two doses are equivalent.
cases.evidence_text: Pilot randomized study (N=56, 28 per arm): mean difference in symptom score = -0.18 (SE = 0.24, 95% CI -0.65 to 0.29, p = 0.45). Prespecified practical equivalence margin is [-0.30, +0.30].

cases.title: Best-of-24 hyperparameter/seed sweeps reported as externally generalizable gain
cases.question: Does architecture A generalize better than baseline B on unseen benchmarks?
cases.draft: Architecture A outperforms baseline B with macro-F1 = 0.91 across diverse real-world datasets.
cases.evidence_text: Evaluated 24 hyperparameter and random-seed forks on internal dev split; best fork reached macro-F1 = 0.91 (baseline single run 0.87). No held-out external benchmark or multiplicity correction was applied.

cases.title: Strong multi-state DiD + placebo check falsely balanced against unadjusted cross-section
cases.question: Did policy P reduce emergency readmission rates in adopting states?
cases.draft: On the one hand, the 18-state DiD with placebo controls shows a -4.2 pp reduction; on the other hand, a single-hospital unadjusted survey saw no change. Both views have merit and more research is needed.
cases.evidence_text: Staggered difference-in-differences across 18 adopting vs 20 control states (2019-2025): ATT = -4.2 percentage points (95% CI -6.4 to -2.0, p = 0.0002); pre-trends parallel (joint F p = 0.61); negative-control surgical placebo ATT = -0.1 pp (p = 0.79).

hypotheses.statement: Policy P reduced readmissions by ~4.2 pp
No policy effect based on unadjusted single-hospital snapshot

cases.title: Double-blind RCT 2x2 event reduction falsely hedged as inconclusive
cases.question: Does prophylaxis regimen R reduce post-operative infection incidence?
cases.draft: On the one hand, the RCT showed 42/260 vs 74/260 infections; on the other hand, historical anecdotes were mixed. More studies are needed to re-evaluate in the future.
cases.evidence_text: Double-blind multicenter RCT (N=520): post-operative infections occurred in 42/260 treated vs 74/260 control patients (RR = 0.5676, 95% CI 0.4050 to 0.7954, Fisher exact p = 0.0010).

cases.title: Target-trial observational emulation with high E-value and clean negative control
cases.question: Does statin initiation reduce 5-year MACE under target-trial emulation?
cases.draft: In the target-trial emulation (N=8,400), statin initiation conditionally reduces 5-year MACE (HR = 0.58, 95% CI 0.49 to 0.69) assuming no unmeasured confounder stronger than E-value 2.26.
cases.evidence_text: Target-trial emulated cohort (N=8,400 adults, IPW + active comparator): 5-year MACE HR = 0.58 (95% CI 0.49 to 0.69, p < 0.0001); negative-control outcome accidental trauma HR = 1.01 (95% CI 0.87 to 1.17, p = 0.89).

cases.title: Well-powered equivalence RCT passing TOST within prespecified margin
cases.question: Is generic formulation G bioequivalent to reference drug R within [-0.15, +0.15]?
cases.draft: In the N=1,200 equivalence trial, mean difference = 0.02 (SE = 0.05) falls strictly inside [-0.15, +0.15] (TOST p = 0.0047), establishing practical equivalence.
cases.evidence_text: Multicenter randomized equivalence trial (N=1,200): mean difference = 0.02 (SE = 0.05, 90% CI -0.062 to 0.102), prespecified equivalence bounds [-0.15, +0.15], TOST p = 0.0047.

cases.title: Heterogeneous overlapping observational meta-analysis genuinely insufficient
cases.question: Does pooled observational evidence establish an effect of exposure E on outcome Y?
cases.draft: Pooling 5 observational cohorts (OR = 1.14, 95% CI 0.88 to 1.48, I^2 = 78%, overlapping registries) is insufficient to establish an effect.
cases.evidence_text: Random-effects meta-analysis of 5 observational cohorts (k=5, partial sample overlap across 2 registries): pooled OR = 1.14 (95% CI 0.88 to 1.48, p = 0.32, I^2 = 78%).

cases.title: Unit tests and reproduced latency speedup overclaimed as user impact
cases.question: Does the new caching layer improve real user outcomes?
cases.draft: All 380 tests pass and median latency drops 18% (95% CI -22% to -14%) across 5 runs, proving superior user impact in production.
cases.evidence_text: CI test log: 380/380 unit tests passed. Replicated benchmark across 5 independent runs: median query latency change = -18.0% (95% CI -22.0% to -14.0%). No production user telemetry collected.
